title: Identification of COVID-19 spread mechanisms based on first-wave data, simulation models, and evolutionary algorithms.
summary: Across 61 countries, modified SEIR fit better than classical SEIR in 43; Bass diffusion beat SI in 57. The fitted models support an additional spread component not directly dependent on contact with infected individuals. Compared model fits across 61 countries; report gives Mann–Whitney U comparisons. Evidence is retrospective curve fit, not causal identification.

source_review.scope: Read the PLOS primary article, including Methods and Results. L-SHADE differential evolution (an evolutionary optimization algorithm) tuned SI/SIR/SEIR-family and Bass-diffusion model parameters to first-wave COVID-19 data for 61 countries. The modified SEIR fit outperformed classical SEIR in 43/61 countries and the Bass-diffusion model outperformed SI in 57; the authors infer a model component for spread not directly dependent on contact with infected individuals. PLOS reports publication on 2022-12-28. DOI/title/result are absent from both supplied active and archived catalog snapshots. Caveat: model fitting to first-wave cumulative cases supports a model-dependent hypothesis, not causal proof of a transmission route.
